title: Project Class Schedule: Entry Values, Surveys and Estimate Validity
content:
# Project Class Schedule — Entry Values, Surveys and Estimate Validity

Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects are written in six project classes. Each class is written for a smallest project value, states whether a site survey of the existing system is required before the estimate is issued and whether engineering and design of the replacement are included in the class, holds the estimate open for award for a stated number of calendar days, and holds the quoted equipment price for a stated number of calendar days before a supplier escalation is passed through.

## Schedule

| Project class | Smallest project value (USD) | Site survey required before the estimate | Engineering and design included | Design fee where not included (per cent of contract value) | Estimate validity (calendar days) | Equipment price held (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Equipment Replacement Order | 4500 | no | no | 0 | 30 | 30 |
| Planned Replacement Program | 25000 | yes | no | 4 | 45 | 45 |
| Controls Retrofit Project | 40000 | yes | yes | 0 | 45 | 60 |
| Energy Retrofit Project | 75000 | yes | yes | 0 | 60 | 60 |
| Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project | 250000 | yes | yes | 0 | 60 | 45 |
| Design-Build Infrastructure Program | 750000 | yes | yes | 0 | 90 | 45 |

## Reading the schedule

1. The entry gate of a class is its smallest project value together with its survey and design settings: a scope reaches a class when the estimated contract value is at least the smallest project value shown for it.
2. The estimate validity and the equipment price hold are separate clocks. Both are counted in calendar days; the first governs how long the estimate stays open for award, the second how long the quoted equipment price stands before a supplier escalation is passed through. In the Controls Retrofit Project the price hold (60 days) is longer than the estimate validity (45 days); in the Turnkey Mechanical Upgrade Project and the Design-Build Infrastructure Program it is shorter (45 days against 60 and 90).
3. The design fee is charged only in the one class that neither includes engineering and design nor is written without it as a matter of course: the Planned Replacement Program carries a design fee of 4 per cent of the contract value. Every class that includes engineering and design shows a fee of 0, as does the Equipment Replacement Order, which is written without a design stage.

## Illustrative reading (hypothetical scope)

A scope estimated at USD 60000 reaches the Controls Retrofit Project (smallest value 40000) and does not reach the Energy Retrofit Project (smallest value 75000). Written at the Controls Retrofit Project, its estimate stays open for 45 calendar days and its equipment price is held for 60 calendar days.
